clauses.reason: The order exempts Henry L. Schmidt, senior power plant operative, Government Printing Office, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and fixes the period in its own words: "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1942". The end is recorded as January 31, 1942 (1942-01-31), inclusive: the exemption runs through that day. The exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative. EO 9016, signed January 12, 1942, cites this order by number ("Executive Order No. 8626 of ") and exempts the same employee again: "I hereby further exempt" ... "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1943". It states no separate effective date, so its signature date is recorded as the event date. It is a later event, not an end: it is a new exemption for a later period and does not revoke, shorten or supersede the exemption in EO 8626.

"for a period of one year ending January 31, 1943". It states no separate effective date, so its signature date is recorded as the event date. It is a later event, not an end: it is a new exemption for a later period and does not revoke, shorten or supersede the exemption in EO 8626. Schmidt rendered while the exemption was in force is a completed fact that the end of the period does not undo; that is the only effect that outlasts the order.
